title: Resilient & Decoupled Architectures
oneLiner: Build systems that bend without breaking: multi-AZ, load balancing, auto scaling, and async decoupling.
examWeightNote: Part of Design Resilient Architectures (26% of the exam).
objectives: Use Elastic Load Balancing and EC2 Auto Scaling to add fault tolerance and elasticity.
Decouple components with Amazon SQS, SNS, and EventBridge so failures don't cascade.
Choose between ALB, NLB, and GLB for the right layer and protocol.
Design stateless tiers so instances can be added or replaced freely.

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.purpose: Distributes traffic across healthy targets in multiple AZs; ALB (L7), NLB (L4), GLB (appliances).

services.name: EC2 Auto Scaling
services.purpose: Adds/removes instances to match demand and replaces unhealthy ones automatically.

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.purpose: Fully managed message queue that buffers work between producers and consumers.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.purpose: Pub/sub fan-out to many subscribers (queues, Lambda, HTTP, email).

services.name: Amazon EventBridge
services.purpose: Event bus that routes events between AWS services and apps using rules.

keyConcepts: Put an Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer spanning multiple AZs — the ASG replaces failed instances and scales on demand; the ELB routes only to healthy targets.
SQS decouples producers from consumers: if consumers slow down or fail, messages wait in the queue instead of being lost (buffering / load leveling).
SNS fans out one message to many subscribers; combine SNS + SQS (fan-out pattern) so each service gets its own durable queue.
Use an ALB for HTTP/HTTPS (path/host routing), an NLB for extreme performance / TCP-UDP / static IP, and a Gateway Load Balancer for third-party virtual appliances.
Keep application tiers stateless (store session/state in DynamoDB or ElastiCache) so any instance can handle any request and scaling is painless.

scenarios.scenario: An order-processing service calls a downstream inventory service synchronously. When inventory is slow, orders time out and are lost, and traffic spikes overwhelm the downstream service.
scenarios.question: Which change best decouples the two services and prevents lost orders during spikes?

options.label: Place an Amazon SQS queue between them so orders buffer and are processed at a steady rate
Increase the timeout on the synchronous call
Move both services onto one larger EC2 instance
Enable Multi-AZ on the downstream service only

scenarios.explanation: An SQS queue decouples producer and consumer: orders are durably buffered and the downstream service pulls at its own pace (load leveling), so spikes don't cause lost orders or overload.

scenarios.scenario: A web tier must automatically recover from instance failures and handle daily traffic peaks without manual intervention, spread across two AZs.
scenarios.question: Which combination meets the requirement?

options.label: A single large EC2 instance with a static Elastic IP
An Auto Scaling group across two AZs behind an Application Load Balancer
Two instances in one AZ without a load balancer
A Lambda function triggered by CloudWatch alarms

scenarios.explanation: An ASG across multiple AZs behind an ALB replaces unhealthy instances automatically and scales with demand, while the ALB routes traffic only to healthy targets — the classic resilient web-tier pattern.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of placing an SQS queue between a producer and a consumer?
options: It encrypts the messages with a customer key
It decouples them so the consumer can process at its own pace and messages aren't lost during spikes
It provides a public HTTP endpoint
It automatically scales the consumer's CPU
quiz.answer: It decouples them so the consumer can process at its own pace and messages aren't lost during spikes
quiz.explanation: SQS buffers messages (load leveling), decoupling components so a slow or failed consumer doesn't drop work or overwhelm downstream systems.

quiz.question: Which load balancer should you use for HTTP path-based and host-based routing at layer 7?
quiz.explanation: The ALB operates at layer 7 and supports content-based routing (path, host, headers). The NLB is layer 4 for ultra-high performance/TCP-UDP; GLB is for virtual appliances.

quiz.question: What does EC2 Auto Scaling do when an instance fails its health check?
options: Sends an email and waits for manual action
Terminates the unhealthy instance and launches a replacement
quiz.answer: Terminates the unhealthy instance and launches a replacement
quiz.explanation: Auto Scaling maintains the desired capacity by replacing unhealthy instances automatically, improving resilience.

quiz.question: You need to deliver a single event to multiple independent subscribers, each with its own durable buffer. What is the recommended pattern?
options: SNS fan-out to multiple SQS queues
A single SQS queue polled by all subscribers
Direct synchronous HTTP calls to each subscriber
Storing events in an EBS volume
quiz.answer: SNS fan-out to multiple SQS queues
quiz.explanation: The SNS + SQS fan-out pattern publishes one message to an SNS topic that delivers to several SQS queues, giving each consumer its own durable copy to process independently.

quiz.question: When would you choose a Network Load Balancer over an Application Load Balancer?
options: For ultra-low latency, millions of requests/sec, TCP/UDP, or a static IP requirement
quiz.answer: For ultra-low latency, millions of requests/sec, TCP/UDP, or a static IP requirement
quiz.explanation: The NLB operates at layer 4 for extreme performance and TCP/UDP workloads, and provides a static IP per AZ. The ALB is the layer-7 choice for HTTP content-based routing.

quiz.question: Which SQS queue type guarantees exactly-once processing and preserves message order?
quiz.explanation: FIFO queues preserve ordering and provide exactly-once processing (at reduced throughput). Standard queues offer higher throughput with at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering.

quiz.question: What is the role of a load balancer health check in a resilient architecture?
options: It routes traffic only to targets that are responding correctly, avoiding unhealthy ones
quiz.answer: It routes traffic only to targets that are responding correctly, avoiding unhealthy ones
quiz.explanation: Health checks let the load balancer detect unhealthy targets and stop sending them traffic, so users aren't routed to failing instances.

quiz.question: Why should application-tier EC2 instances be kept stateless where possible?
options: So any instance can handle any request, making scaling and instance replacement seamless
Because stateful apps are not allowed on AWS
To reduce the number of AZs required to one
quiz.answer: So any instance can handle any request, making scaling and instance replacement seamless
quiz.explanation: Storing session/state externally (e.g. DynamoDB or ElastiCache) keeps instances stateless, so Auto Scaling can add or replace them freely without losing user state.

quiz.question: Which service is best suited to route events from many AWS services and apps to targets based on rules?
quiz.explanation: EventBridge is a serverless event bus that matches events against rules and routes them to targets like Lambda, SQS, and Step Functions — ideal for event-driven, decoupled architectures.
